review_scope: Author self-check only, bound to exact authored bytes. Not independent review, human approval, a candidate answer, or formal verification.
assumption_checks: K is finite abstract simplicial, v is a vertex and B is an actual subcomplex containing v.
The punctured realization is explicitly nonempty and contractible; no compactness or closed-subcomplex status is attributed to it.
The punctured B inclusion being a homotopy equivalence excludes isolated v by path-component surjectivity, hence link has a vertex.
Every realization uses two finite cones and a genuine closed edge B; punctured edge inclusion has an explicit homotopy inverse.
proof_checks: Barycentric normalization is continuous on O, remains in each original simplex, fixes the deletion, and is never extended across v.
Only the closed deletion subcomplex is collapsed using its CW homotopy extension property; the quotient is the unreduced suspension of the link.
Reduced integral suspension homology handles degree zero and torsion. Acyclicity gives path-connected link before van Kampen is applied.
The contractible conclusion uses simple connectivity, Hurewicz and Whitehead for CW complexes; it is not inferred from arbitrary acyclicity.
The finite augmented chain complex is recoverable from the local incident-face data and decidable by integer matrix normal forms.
The optional balanced presentation has determinant 1, while explicit A5 permutations certify nontrivial fundamental group; the finite simplicial model theorem applies.
The type-range theorem neither assumes nor concludes that suspension reflects homotopy equivalence.
source_checks: Original 2003 published proof context, Mnev 2007 version 3, and author 2009 erratum were read.
Only an acknowledged proof gap is attributed to the historical source; no disproof of the original theorem or full present-day status claim is made.
Replacement of the original matroid posets by arbitrary finite complexes and replacement of the deleted subcomplex by one vertex are explicit independent adaptations.
